narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Back of the Box"**

The page at `palawi.fr/polaris/` is printed on the back insert of Polaris's retail box. One cardinal red carries the whole card, with only two inks printed on it: cream and a deep red-brown. The big screenshot is not a picture. It is the live terminal game in a cream-bordered frame. Before play, a printed capture of the title screen sits exactly on the terminal's cells. Pressing the cream sticker cuts that capture away, and the running game is underneath, already showing the same title and prompt.

Density is a retail box's: one dominant screenshot, a narrow column of three feature blurbs, each with a real ASCII monster from the game, then a spec strip, a controls list and the small print with a barcode. The controls behave like hardware. Cream keys rest proud of the card, sink 2px when pressed and lie flat when the game is not listening. The warm near-black screen is the most saturated, highest-contrast area of the page. Everything printed on the red stays quieter than it.

The system rejects the neon or glow "gamer" look: no black page around a centred terminal, and no luminous halos.
keyCharacteristics: One printed red ground under a faint red-brown halftone dot (4px pitch), lighter toward the top.
Two inks on the red: cream and red-brown. The screen is the only dark, high-contrast area.
The title is the game's own ░▒▓█ block lettering, generated from the game source and never typeset in a font.
Controls have real travel: they rest, sink when pressed, and flatten when the game is not listening.
Printed rules are hairlines: 1px, and 0.5px on 2x screens.
One signature move: the printed capture is clipped away left to right to show the live game.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Anything printed on the red uses only cream (at full strength or as soft cream, or as alpha rules) and red-brown. A third ink is not allowed. This is why the small logo keeps only the solid █ cells and drops the shaded tints.

rules.name: The Live Screen Rule
rules.body: The terminal is the most saturated, highest-contrast area of the page (15.8:1). Printed areas on the red stay at about 5 to 6:1.

rules.name: The Game Letters Rule
rules.body: "POLARIS" is always the game's own block art from `internal/game/game.go`, rendered by `scripts/logo.mjs` as crisp-edged SVG cells (3×6 units). The flap logo keeps only the solid █ cells. The printed capture draws ▓▒░ as the same 4×8 ordered dither (75/50/25%) that `scripts/blocks_font.py` bakes into "Polaris Blocks", so the print and the live terminal show identical dots.

rules.name: The Mono Stays On Screen Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only on screen surfaces: the terminal, the capture's prompt line, the ASCII vignettes and the error detail. Copy on the red is never set in mono.

rules.name: The Fixed Numerals Rule
rules.body: Keypad digits, `kbd` caps and the save line use tabular numerals so they keep fixed positions.

rules.name: The Ninety Columns Rule
rules.body: The terminal font size is computed so that 92 columns fit (`floor(width / 92 / 0.6)`, clamped to 10–16px), then the fit addon fills the frame. The 86-column title is never scaled by CSS inside the live terminal.

rules.name: The Falling Light Rule
rules.body: Shadows always fall downward and are tinted with the ink of the surface below. A zero-offset, wide-blur shadow is a glow, and the system has none. (The rule is shared with the palawi.fr hub.)

rules.name: The Real Travel Rule
rules.body: A pressed control moves `translateY(2px)` and switches to the key-down shadow. On fine pointers only, hover lifts it 1px (2px for the sticker). The toggled states (sound off, fullscreen on) hold the pressed position. When the game is not waiting for input, the keypad keys sit 2px down, lose their shadow and drop to 55% opacity. They flatten into the card instead of greying out.

rules.name: The One Device Pixel Rule
rules.body: Printed rules (flap, spec strip borders, controls rows, small-print top) use the `--rule` width: 1px, or 0.5px at 2dppx and above, always in cream at 45–60% alpha. Frames are not rules. They are thick cream borders.

rules.name: The Cell Grid Rule
rules.body: Anything printed over the live screen is positioned in terminal cells, never in arbitrary pixels, so when the cut passes the live screen continues the print without a jump.

rules.name: The One Sticker Rule
rules.body: Each print carries exactly one sticker, and it is the only primary action on the page.

dos: **Do** print everything on the red in the two inks (cream and red-brown), and keep the terminal as the only high-contrast area.
**Do** render "POLARIS" only from the game's block art via `scripts/logo.mjs`: solid cells for small sizes, the 4×8 dither for the printed capture.
**Do** place anything laid over the live terminal on measured cells (`--cw`, `--ch`, `--px`, `--py`), and reveal the game with the clip-path cut-away (560ms, cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)).
**Do** give every control real travel: the key shadow at rest, 2px down with the key-down shadow when pressed, and flat at 55% when the game is not listening.
**Do** draw printed rules with `--rule` in cream at 45–60% alpha.
**Do** keep tabular numerals on keys, `kbd` caps and the save line.
**Do** frame every screen surface in solid cream with soft corners and a downward shadow tinted in red-brown.
donts: **Don't** put the game in a dark page with a centred terminal window and a generic play button. The page is the red box.
**Don't** use neon, glow, or zero-offset luminous halos. Shadows fall downward.
**Don't** typeset the title in a font, or print the ▓▒░ tints as a third ink on the red.
**Don't** use JetBrains Mono for copy on the red. Mono belongs to screen surfaces.
**Don't** show a picture of the game where the live game can run. Vignettes are the game's real ASCII art, not mock-ups.
**Don't** add a second sticker or competing primary action to a print.
**Don't** add uppercase labels above headings. The flap genre line is the only small uppercase line, and it sits beside the logo.
**Don't** print ratings, review quotes or player counts on the box.
